assessment.summary: ABL1 is one of the most extensively validated and successfully drugged kinase targets in oncology, with 7 approved drugs, over 5,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 85 high-resolution crystal structures including ligand-bound complexes at sub-angstrom resolution. The target is primarily implicated in BCR-ABL1-driven chronic myeloid leukemia and is supported by a vast and active literature base exceeding 1,200 publications. Druggability confidence is exceptionally high across all dimensions.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 63.4 is relatively low, suggesting disordered regions (likely the N-terminal regulatory and linker regions), but this is not a concern given the wealth of experimental crystal structures
Resistance mutations (e.g., T315I gatekeeper) remain a clinical challenge; coverage of all clinically relevant mutant structures may be incomplete
Regorafenib is listed as an ABL1 inhibitor but is primarily known as a multi-kinase inhibitor; its ABL1-specific clinical relevance is less clear than imatinib/dasatinib/nilotinib/bosutinib
Selectivity profiles across the full kinome for all approved agents are not captured in this dataset
Emerging roles of ABL1 in non-CML contexts (e.g., solid tumors, CHDSKM developmental syndrome) are still being characterised and may require distinct drugging strategies
